description: MYNTS, the Multiphysical Network Simulator, is a software tool developed by Fraunhofer SCAI to analyse and optimise transport networks for gas, electricity, district heat, water and sector coupling through numerical simulation in the planning stage, developed in close collaboration with industrial users such as Open Grid Europe. MYNTS-G/L simulates gas networks, including subnetworks such as compressor stations and mixing chambers, with hydrogen shares up to 100 percent modelled according to GERG-2008, extension to liquid phases such as CO2 transport and dynamic fluid transport; MYNTS-E offers steady-state AC and DC power flow and economic optimal power flow; MYNTS-H covers heating and cooling grids and MYNTS-W water distribution. Features include programmable subnetworks, open modelling, steady-state and time-dependent calculations, efficient kernels for multi-processor computers and visualisation. Access: licences for Windows and Linux on request through a contact form, a trial is offered, and the MYNTS-Reader for viewing grids and scenarios is an open-access download. Cost is not published. Caveats: proprietary software, with heat, water and sector coupling modules still in licensing. It suits gas and hydrogen network planning and security-of-supply studies, and relates to the MYNTS European gas supply security case study catalogued here.
